declared.title: Failure to learn from failure is mitigated by loss-framing and corrective feedback: A replication and test of the boundary conditions of the tune-out effect.
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « failure to learn from failure tune-out effect replication corrective feedback loss framing » (2026-11-23)

population: adults in 2 preregistered experiments (N = 520) repeating the task of Eskreis-Winkler & Fishbach 2019; countries not given in the abstract (authors in Germany)

findings.text: In conditions close to the original study, people again learned less after failure feedback than after success feedback

support.sentence: The tune-out effect fully replicated in those experimental conditions that represented close replications of the original study, underscoring the reliability of the original effect.

findings.text: The gap disappeared when the same money at stake was framed as a loss for each wrong answer instead of a gain for each right one

support.sentence: However, the effect disappeared when the same monetary incentives for participation were expressed in terms of a loss (i.e., losing money for each wrong answer) rather than a gain (i.e., earning money for each correct answer; Experiment 1).

findings.text: The gap also disappeared when people received additional corrective feedback after failing

support.sentence: The effect also disappeared when additional corrective feedback was given (Experiment 2).

limits: the same laboratory task as the original: the scoring critique of Spiller 2025 applies to the close replications
the gap vanishing with corrective feedback or loss framing is also what the consistency artefact predicts when learning rises: it does not separate the two readings
one laboratory, not a multi-lab replication; each boundary condition tested in a single experiment
learning tested within the session, with money incentives; not failures in life
Keith and Frese developed error management training (keith-2008): they replicated an effect against their own view that errors teach, which adds to its credibility
